item.text:
This pass added two more executed checks of the consensus core; both are clean, so the finding set is unchanged.

**New this pass**

- **Randomised multi-node protocol fuzz** (`TestAuditRaftSafetyFuzz`): 3-node and 5-node clusters, 3000 ticks each, 20% message loss, 0–2 tick reordering, and a 60-tick partition every 150 ticks. Per run it produces ~700 proposals, ~20 leader terms and ~650 committed entries, checking every 10 ticks that no two nodes are leader in the same term, that all committed entries agree on term and payload across nodes, and that per-node commit indexes never regress. After healing the network it requires a leader and a newly committed proposal. 20/20 runs pass — no safety or liveness violation.

- **Crash-safety of votes** (`TestAuditVoteSurvivesRestart`): drives a node into candidate state, persists `pb.State` through `Peer.GetUpdate`/`Peer.Commit`, relaunches it from the same LogDB, verifies term/vote are restored, and that a `RequestVote` from another node in the same term is rejected. Passes.

Both are recorded in [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_20-19-30-dragonboat_raft-baseline/work/report.md) under the “reviewed without finding a defect” list, with the new test files and commands added to the inventory and command log.

**Current state**

- Findings remain: F1 `(*nodeUser).ReadIndex` misses the engine wakeup (one-RTT latency; one-RTT timeouts deterministically fail), and F2 `handleCandidateReadIndex` records a dropped ReadIndex twice (visible via `Peer.GetUpdate`).
- Tagged audit run: `PASS` protocol fuzz, `PASS` in-memory model check, `PASS` proposal control, `PASS` vote-restart check; the two Finding-2 tests fail as documented; the F1 test fails only under the audit tag.
- Default suites stay green, and the implementation is byte-identical to `../source`.

Remaining useful work: mutual-TLS transport paths (blocked on the missing `tests/localhost.key`), an executable `tools.ImportSnapshot` repair scenario, and a mutant-style sweep of the root package for further sibling-method deviations like Finding 1.
